title: Two Hundred Hours: The Unfashionable Price of a Close Friend
title_zh: 两百个小时：一个挚友背后并不时髦的代价
intro_zh: 本文约 516 词，围绕“友谊在生活中的意义”展开：用研究数据说明友谊是如何被一点点“用时间造出来”的，并解释为什么我们常常不敢联系老朋友。文中含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度中等，理解目标约 85%-90%。

paragraphs.en: No one introduces a close friend by saying, 'We spent two hundred hours together.' Yet that is roughly the price. In a study at the University of Kansas, researchers asked more than 350 adults to look back at a friendship and describe how it had grown. The answers turned a mysterious process into simple arithmetic: turning a stranger into a casual friend took about 50 hours of shared time, reaching 'friend' took around 90, and reaching 'close friend' took more than 200.
paragraphs.zh: 没有人在介绍一位挚友时会说：“我们一共相处了两百个小时。”可这恰恰就是代价。在堪萨斯大学的一项研究中，研究者请350多名成年人回想一段友谊，并描述它是如何发展起来的。答案把一个神秘的过程变成了简单的算术：把一个陌生人变成普通朋友，大约需要共处50个小时；成为“朋友”约需90个小时；而成为“挚友”则需要200小时以上。

paragraphs.en: Most of those hours were not dramatic at all. They were cups of tea, walks to the bus stop, waiting together for a delayed train, or sitting in the same room saying nothing. The researchers found that the activities mattered far less than the repetition. Friendship does not tend to grow out of one perfect evening; it grows out of many small evenings that nobody planned to remember.
paragraphs.zh: 这些时间大多一点也不戏剧化：几杯茶、一起走到公交站、一起等一班晚点的火车，或者坐在同一个房间里一言不发。研究者发现，具体做什么远不如“反复”重要。友谊往往不会从一个完美的夜晚里长出来，而是从许多谁也没打算记住的普通夜晚里长出来。

paragraphs.en: Time alone, of course, explains only part of the story. Since 1938, the Harvard Study of Adult Development has followed hundreds of people and their families, tracking jobs, health and marriages. Its best-known conclusion is that the quality of close relationships predicts happiness and physical health better than money, fame or career success. People who maintain warm connections live longer and report more satisfaction with their lives.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，单靠时间只能解释故事的一部分。自1938年起，“哈佛成人发展研究”追踪了数百人及其家人，记录他们的工作、健康和婚姻。它最著名的结论是：亲密关系的质量对幸福和身体健康的预测力，超过金钱、名望或事业成功。那些维持着温暖关系的人活得更久，对生活的满意度也更高。

paragraphs.en: So why do so many of us stop calling? One reason is a quiet misjudgment. In a series of experiments, psychologists found that after a conversation, people consistently underestimated how much the other person had liked them. We remember our own awkward sentences; the other side remembers a pleasant half hour. That gap between how we think we appear and how we are actually seen keeps many friendships from ever starting.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，为什么我们这么多人会不再打电话？一个原因是一种无声的误判。在一系列实验中，心理学家发现，一次交谈之后，人们总是低估对方对自己的好感。我们记着自己那些笨拙的句子，对方记住的却是一个愉快的半小时。我们以为自己给人的印象，与别人实际看到的印象之间的这道差距，让许多友谊根本没能开始。

paragraphs.en: A 2022 study added a second twist. When people were asked to reach out to someone they had lost touch with, they hesitated, guessing that the message would seem strange or unwelcome. Those who did send it found that the receivers appreciated it far more than expected. The fear of being a burden is usually imaginary.
paragraphs.zh: 2022年的一项研究又添了第二个转折。当人们被要求去联系一位久未往来的旧识时，他们会犹豫，猜想这条消息会显得奇怪或不受欢迎。而那些真的发出消息的人发现，对方远比想象中更感激。怕给别人添麻烦的担忧，多半是自己想出来的。

paragraphs.en: The cost of that fear is visible in the data. In a 2021 survey of American adults, 12 percent said they had no close friends at all, up from 3 percent in 1990. The middle of life is especially risky: work, children and moving house break the weekly rhythms that once kept people close, and loneliness creeps in without any single dramatic event. Nobody notices the last time they meet a friend for lunch.
paragraphs.zh: 这种恐惧的代价在数据里看得见。在2021年一项针对美国成年人的调查中，12%的人说自己一个挚友也没有，而1990年这个比例是3%。中年尤其危险：工作、孩子和搬家打破了曾让人彼此亲近的每周节奏，孤独在没有任何戏剧性事件的情况下悄悄潜入。没有人会注意到自己“最后一次和朋友吃午饭”是哪一天。

paragraphs.en: The good news is that the repair is small. A fifteen-minute phone call, a shared walk on Sunday morning, a message that mentions a detail from last year - these are the materials of genuine friendship. Researchers suggest one practical rule: put the person on the calendar, not just in your heart. Regular, predictable contact does more than intense, rare contact.
paragraphs.zh: 好消息是，修补所需的动作很小。一通十五分钟的电话、周日早上一起散步、一条提到去年某个细节的消息——这些都是真诚友谊的原料。研究者给出了一条实用规则：把这个人写进日程表，而不只是放在心上。规律、可预期的联系，比强烈却稀少的联系更有效。

paragraphs.en: Friendship, then, is less a lucky discovery than a slow craft. It pays clear benefits - lower stress, better health, a longer life - but it asks for something unglamorous in return: hours. Nobody inherits a close friend. Someone has to keep showing up, one ordinary afternoon at a time.
paragraphs.zh: 这样看来，友谊与其说是一次幸运的发现，不如说是一门缓慢的手艺。它带来明显的益处——更低的压力、更好的健康、更长的寿命——但它索取的回报并不光鲜：时间。没有人能继承一位挚友。总得有人一次次出现，一个平常的下午接着一个平常的下午。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why Americans today have fewer hobbies than before.
How friendship is built through time and kept alive by small, regular efforts.
The health risks of living alone in big cities.
How to make a good first impression on strangers.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文以堪萨斯大学“50/90/200小时”研究为线索，说明友谊是靠时间累积而成的，并指出规律的小举动（打电话、散步、发消息）能维持友谊，故选B。A、C、D均只是文中细节或未提及。

questions.q: According to the University of Kansas study, how long does it take to turn a stranger into a close friend?
questions.explain: 细节题。第一段明确写道 reaching 'close friend' took more than 200 hours（成为挚友需要200小时以上）。50小时对应“普通朋友”，90小时对应“朋友”，350是受访人数，故选C。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the 2022 study about contacting an old friend?
options: Unexpected messages are usually refused by the receivers.
We tend to overestimate how welcome our message will be.
Our worry about bothering others is mostly unnecessary.
Only very close friends enjoy hearing from us.
questions.explain: 推断题。第五段指出，人们犹豫是因为担心消息显得奇怪或不受欢迎，但真正发出消息的人发现对方远比预期更感激，可见“怕给别人添麻烦”多半是想象出来的，故选C。B与文意相反。

questions.q: The phrase 'creeps in' in Paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。creep 意为“悄悄移动、蹑手蹑脚地走”，结合语境“孤独在没有任何戏剧性事件的情况下……”可知指孤独缓慢而无声地侵入，故选B。
